summary.text: Son of Hippasus (`hippasus-trojan`) and own brother of wealthy Socus, whom Agamemnon smote with a thrust of his spear when the king raged among the Trojans — distinct from Charops husband of Oia in Attic genealogies.

story.text: Agamemnon let be the warriors he had already laid low and smote Charops son of Hippasus with a thrust of his spear, even the own brother of wealthy Socus. To bear Charops aid came Socus, a godlike man, who took his stand close to Odysseus and wounded the spearman before the twain Aiantes bore him away.
